Is it possible to obtain a Medical Certificate for Food Poisoning digitally?

Yes. DrCertificate connects people in 10 South East Asian countries with certified MBBS, MD or MS doctors, who may issue a food poisoning medical certificate after a digital chat. Issuing is at the doctor's discretion. Approved certificates arrive as a PDF by email. Limits apply: non emergency cases only, and no use in India, for legal matters or for insurance.
Before you apply
What is a medical certificate for food poisoning?

A medical certificate for food poisoning is a document from a certified doctor stating that, after a consultation, you were judged unfit for work or study, or needed to work from home, for a set period. Employers and universities usually ask for one when you miss work or classes.
The certificate records the doctor's decision after a chat consultation, and DrCertificate itself does not diagnose, treat or prescribe.
For food poisoning, the sick leave option is the usual choice. A work from home note suits a person well enough to work but not to travel to the office or campus.
The certificate goes to whoever asked for it, most often an employer, HR team or university office.
Which kinds of food poisoning can a doctor consider online?

A doctor can consider the common, milder forms of food poisoning online, where symptoms are typical and you can still keep fluids down. The doctor reads your description, then decides whether a certificate fits and for how long. No number of days is promised before that review.

The period of rest is the doctor's call. A toxin can cause vomiting that settles within a day, while a bacterial infection can take longer to clear. The NHS says food poisoning is rarely serious and usually gets better within a week. Your symptoms, their timing and how you are coping all shape the decision. Nothing about the length is fixed in advance.
Not every case belongs in a chat.
Bloody diarrhoea, signs of severe dehydration or symptoms that keep getting worse need a doctor who can examine you in person.

items: Bacterial food poisoning Linked to bacteria like Salmonella, Campylobacter or E. Coli. Diarrhoea, cramps, vomiting and fever are common.
Viral stomach bug Norovirus spreads through contaminated food and close contact, with sudden vomiting and watery diarrhoea.
Toxin food poisoning Toxins from Staphylococcus aureus in food can cause sudden vomiting within hours that often passes quickly.
Traveller's diarrhoea Loose stools and cramps after contaminated food or water while away from home.

blocks.text: What should you tell the doctor about your food poisoning?
Tell the doctor which symptoms you have, when they started, how severe they are and the leave period you are asking for. Clear, honest details help the doctor reach a decision.
Your name and ID details must match, or the request can be declined.

items: Symptoms Vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach cramps or fever.
Onset and duration The date symptoms began and whether they are easing.
Severity How often you vomit or pass loose stools, and whether you can keep fluids down.
Reports Any clinic notes or test results you already have.
Leave requested The dates you need the certificate to cover.

blocks.text: When is food poisoning not suitable for an online certificate?

Food poisoning is not suitable for an online certificate when warning signs point to a more serious illness. The NHS tells people in the UK to call its 111 service straight away for the signs below. In South East Asia, see a doctor in person or call local emergency services.
DrCertificate is only for suitable non emergency situations. The platform does not diagnose, treat or prescribe, and a doctor may decline any request that cannot be handled safely by chat.

items: Constant vomiting You keep being sick and cannot keep fluid down.
Blood You have bloody diarrhoea or bleeding from the bottom.
Long lasting diarrhoea Diarrhoea has gone on for more than 7 days.
Long lasting vomiting Vomiting has gone on for more than 2 days.

What happens if the doctor does not issue a certificate for food poisoning?
If the doctor does not issue a certificate, you do not receive one and the payment is not refunded. Each doctor makes an independent decision based on what you share.

blocks.text: Questions about medical certificates for food poisoning
Can I share test results or reports for food poisoning?

Yes, you can mention any test results, clinic notes or reports in the details you give on the form. Tests are not always needed for food poisoning, but sharing what you already have gives the doctor a fuller picture. Keep every detail accurate, since inconsistent information is a common reason for a decline.
How long can a food poisoning sick leave certificate cover?

The doctor decides the leave period after the chat, based on your symptoms. In most South East Asian countries, sick leave and work from home notes go up to 7 days for generic symptoms. The NHS says food poisoning usually gets better within a week, and shorter periods are common.
Will my employer accept an online medical certificate?

Acceptance is decided by your employer or institution, not by DrCertificate. All doctors on the platform are registered with a medical council, but workplace and university rules differ. Check with HR or your school office that online medical notes are accepted before you apply, because payments are non refundable.
Can I have a video call or see the doctor in person?

No. DrCertificate does not offer video or in person consultations. The doctor reviews your request through a digital chat consultation only. If you feel your food poisoning needs a physical examination, visit a local clinic or hospital instead of applying online.
What should I do if my food poisoning symptoms get worse?

Seek in person medical care straight away if food poisoning gets worse. Go to a clinic or hospital if you cannot keep fluids down, notice blood in your stool, or have diarrhoea beyond 7 days or vomiting beyond 2 days. In an emergency, call your local emergency number.
How fast will I receive my food poisoning certificate?

Approved certificates usually arrive by email as a PDF in about 30 minutes. The doctor first reviews your form and completes the chat consultation. A certificate cannot be corrected once issued unless the fault came from the medical team, so check your name, ID and dates before you submit.
